name: マーカー付きの導入文
prompt:
Create a clean 1179 x 449 px Japanese editorial introduction component on a white canvas. Use the first reference as the authority for the visual composition: large, near-black editorial serif lettering, left aligned, with a separate pale sage-green marker rectangle behind each line. Keep the rectangles flat, subtle, and closely fitted to each line with only a small inset; preserve the source's simple high-contrast style, broad white background, and no card frame or decoration. Use the second reference only for the already-authored Japanese copy. Set the exact wording below, on exactly three lines, with no added or missing characters:
ここは、考えや体験を分かち合う場所。
多様な声が出会うことで、
新しい理解が生まれます。
Keep the line block left aligned around x=77 px and vertically centered, with generous but even leading. Use clear Japanese glyphs at a substantial size similar to the reference's English text. The first highlight strip should be widest, and the second and third should end naturally with their shorter lines. Do not add the Medium logo, other text, shadows, borders, gradients, imagery, or page content.
reviewNotes: Source and candidate were inspected side by side. The exact three-line copy from the native Japanese preview is legible; the separate pale sage marker strips preserve the source serif style. Japanese localization uses three rows versus four in the English source; the text block center is within 5 px of the source block center and the first strip is within 13 px of source width. Generated output normalized to 1179x449.
reviewNotice: 画像生成候補。ネイティブ編集・実装・所有者承認とは別です。
